meta.title: San Martin's Bridge in Toledo: How to Visit, History and Best Views
meta.description: Guide to San Martin's Bridge in Toledo with location, how to get there, history, best viewpoints, photos and practical visiting tips.

hero.title: San Martin's Bridge
hero.subtitle: 14th-century pedestrian bridge with sweeping views of the Tagus River

about.title: About the bridge
about.description: San Martin’s Bridge crosses the Tagus west of Toledo. It already existed in the 14th century, and its profile comprises five pointed arches and two hexagonal towers. Declared a National Monument in 1921, it reveals the relationship between the river, the walls and the medieval approach to the city.

highlights.title: Highlights
items: Panoramic views of the Tagus River and Toledo city
Ideal photography spot to capture Toledo's essence
Historic connection between Tagus River banks

visitPlanning.title: Before You Visit San Martin's Bridge
items: Allow around 20–40 minutes for the walk and views; this is an editorial suggestion to adjust to your pace.
Combine the bridge with San Juan de los Reyes and Santa María la Blanca, visiting timed indoor spaces first.
Check the map before setting out and allow for slopes and stone paving.
Bring water and sun protection as the weather requires, and choose photographs around the day’s light.

items.title: Medieval Architecture
items.description: Admire the impressive Gothic architecture of the bridge with its five arches of different sizes. The medieval construction demonstrates the mastery of 14th-century architects and their ability to adapt to the rocky Tagus terrain.

items.title: Panoramic Tagus River Views
items.description: From the bridge you can enjoy the best views of the Tagus River and its meander that surrounds the city of Toledo. The natural landscape perfectly combines with the historic architecture of the city.

items.title: Photography and Viewpoints
items.description: San Martin's Bridge is an ideal spot for photography, offering multiple angles to capture Toledo's beauty. Sunrise and sunset provide perfect lighting for spectacular photos.

items.title: Connection with History
items.description: Walking across this bridge transports you to medieval times. It has witnessed centuries of Toledan history and continues to be a vital element of the city's cultural heritage.

practical.title: Basic information

hours.label: Opening hours and tickets
hours.value: Free access; no admission ticket is required. Check local conditions before travelling.

transport.label: Getting There
transport.value: The bridge is west of Toledo’s historic centre. Link it on foot with San Juan de los Reyes and the Jewish Quarter, using the map to choose your route.

accessibility.label: Accessibility
accessibility.value: The route includes stone surfaces and changes of level on approach streets. Check any specific mobility requirements before planning your visit.
